Previous lessons:
Helpful changes: Reordering onboarding flow sequences (sign-in after adoption, story-first flow), targeted functional hints (photo upload, path helper, sign-in security), effective layouts (card carousel, single-click identity), specific desktop flows (summon, visibility & control), and quick control redesigns consistently won.
Harmful changes: Desktop docking setup flow, split personality layout redesign, spotlight path selector layout, account persistence hint, and specific copy changes (streamlined path copy, companion name certification copy) significantly hurt performance and led to early test stops.
No clear effect: Wait, progress, and loading indicators, background notifications, tutorial and showcase screens, incentives, and several copy and layout variations showed no clear effect.
Predictions too high: Large predicted gains (+8.5% to +15.0%) consistently overestimated actual impact, frequently yielding smaller gains, no clear effect, or early test cutoffs.
Predictions too low: Major winning tests—especially key desktop flows (visibility & control, summon flow), story-first sequence reordering, card carousel layout, and sign-in security hint—were significantly underestimated.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Helpful changes: Reordering onboarding flow sequences, targeted functional hints (photo upload, path helper, sign-in security), select layouts (card carousel, single-click identity), key desktop flows (summon, visibility & control), and specific shortcut copy changes drove significant wins.

Harmful changes: Major structural redesigns (split personality), intrusive setup flows (desktop docking setup), spotlight path selector layouts, account persistence hints, and specific copy changes caused significant performance drops and early stops.
No clear effect: Wait, progress, and status indicators, background notifications, tutorial/showcase screens, and incentive badges consistently showed no clear effect.
Predictions too high: Large predicted gains (+8.0% and above) consistently overestimated actual performance, frequently resulting in smaller gains, no clear effect, or early test cutoffs.
Predictions too low: Major winning changes—especially shortcut copy, key desktop flows (visibility & control, summon flow), and story-first reordering—far exceeded low or negative predictions.
